title: A complex with projective cohomology has a zero-differential model
statement: Let C be an abelian category, K an integer-indexed cochain complex in C, and assume every homology object H^q(K) is projective [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. There are a cochain complex P with P^q=H^q(K), all differentials zero, and a quasi-isomorphism P to K. No boundedness, freeness of terms, or enough-projectives assumption on C is imposed.

proof.text: For each q split the epimorphism K.cycles(q) to K.homology(q) by projectivity. Define P^q=H^q(K), with zero differential, and define f^q by the section followed by cycles inclusion. The latter is killed by the differential, so f is a chain map. The cycle map of f is the cycles inclusion of P followed by the section. Naturality of homology projections and the section equation show that the composite of homologyMap(f) with the homology projection of P is its cycles inclusion. Both that projection and inclusion are isomorphisms since P has zero differentials, so homologyMap(f) is invertible in each degree. Thus f is a quasi-isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_zero_differential_model_of_projective_homology
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (hK : ∀ q : ℤ, Projective (K.homology q)) :
    ∃ (P : CochainComplex C ℤ) (f : P ⟶ K),
      (∀ q : ℤ, P.X q = K.homology q) ∧
      (∀ i j : ℤ, P.d i j = 0) ∧ QuasiIso f
